solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Withdraw pamphlet after advance payment

indicators.note: the pamphlet word comes after the payment word, so it is placed second

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages, a loan against pay to come
a tract is a short polemical pamphlet

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out of a deal after a leaflet arrives following an upfront payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to take away, deduct or remove an amount, which is what withdrawing a sum does.

clue.text: Left to look into moaning sound coming from shed

indicators.note: the left letter peers inside, so it is placed within the sound word

parts.note: a sough is a moaning or sighing sound, especially of the wind

explanation.surface: A worker turns to investigate an eerie moan coming from a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like an outbuilding but is the verb, as a snake casts off its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To slough is to cast off or discard a layer of skin, which is what shedding means.

clue.text: Tasteless clothes mostly edged with thin type of wool

indicators.note: the clothes letters are bordered on each side by the thin word

parts.note: bony means very thin

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless stuff, especially shabby clothes

explanation.surface: Cheap, gaudy garments trimmed with a fine fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TAT to TA, which is 'edged with' BONY.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany wool is a fine merino wool, named after Botany Bay in Australia.

clue.text: Wandering tribe's resistance mounting on southern island

indicators.note: mounting means climbing, so in this down clue the resistance letter rises to the top

parts.note: a horde was originally a wandering tribe of nomads, such as Tartars
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A nomadic people's resistance grows on an island in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the HORDE piece above S in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the south-eastern Aegean, largest of the Dodecanese.

clue.text: Commonly accepted after vote against acting together

indicators.note: the accepted word goes after the vote word

parts.note: a con is an argument or vote against, as in pros and cons
a current view is one in general circulation, widely accepted

explanation.surface: A popular view prevails after a contrary vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Concurrent means running or operating at the same time, in combination.

clue.text: Calm in city following the introduction of patrols by police

indicators.note: the city comes following the opening letter, so it is placed after it
the introduction of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of patrols is used

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is the standard crossword city
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British plain-clothes detective branch

explanation.surface: A city stays quiet thanks to beat patrols and detective work.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid is a synonym of calm: tranquil, undisturbed, not easily excited.

clue.text: Lear's wrong to bracket it with lines characteristic of scholarly writing

indicators.note: to bracket is to enclose, so the jumbled letters go round the small word
wrong means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the king's name, its four letters taken for rearranging
RY, railway, gives lines in crosswords

explanation.surface: A critic claims King Lear is mistaken to lump something in with scholarly lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges LEAR to LERA, which brackets IT to make LITERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary describes language suited to books and learned prose rather than speech.

clue.text: Clergyman finds a flat close to church

indicators.note: the a-flat pair is placed close to, here just after, the church letters

parts.note: a plain is a flat stretch of land

explanation.surface: A priest finds an apartment near his church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is not an apartment here but level land.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a member of the clergy attached to an institution such as a hospital or regiment.

clue.text: Pulls out eventually edging away from very fast car

parts.note: to drag something is to pull it

indicators.note: eventually points to the end, the final letter
with the edging taken away, only the inner letters remain

explanation.surface: A car eases away from a very speedy vehicle as it pulls out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very fast car' reads as one phrase, but 'very' is wordplay, giving its middle letters ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragster is a car built for drag racing, sprinting at very high speed over a short straight.

clue.text: Departing in spring — not possible earlier

indicators.note: the not-possible word goes earlier, placed in front of the spring word

parts.note: an option that is out is ruled out, not possible
a bound is a spring or leap

explanation.surface: Someone due to leave in springtime finds that an earlier departure cannot be arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Outbound traffic or ships are leaving, heading away from a place, so departing fits.

clue.text: Sarcastic when describing retrogressive levels of society

indicators.note: retrogressive means going backwards, so the assembled letters are read in reverse
describing means drawing a line round, so the when word encloses the sarcastic word

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a tart remark is a sharp, sarcastic one

explanation.surface: Someone is scathing when talking about a society in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means enclosing here, not depicting; 'retrogressive' reverses the whole assembly to make ATARTS read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Social strata are the layers or classes a society is divided into, like geological layers.

clue.text: Make vivacious spice girl take over

parts.note: Ginger Spice, Geri Halliwell, was one of the Spice Girls pop group
up means over or finished, as in 'time's up'

explanation.surface: An instruction to liven things up by having a pop star take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group whose members had nicknames: Ginger, Posh, Baby, Scary and Sporty.
explanation.definitionFit: To ginger up is an idiom for enlivening something, putting energy or spirit into it.

clue.text: Bores doctor with misfortunes

parts.note: ills are troubles or misfortunes

explanation.surface: A tedious doctor who keeps talking about his ailments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' looks like tedious people, but it is the verb: makes holes.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore a hole is to drill one, so bores and drills are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Stop motionless behind bear

indicators.note: in this down clue the motionless word sits behind, below, the bear word

parts.note: to stand something is to bear or tolerate it
still means not moving

explanation.surface: A command to freeze to the spot when a bear is behind you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' is the verb, tolerate, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a complete halt, a stop where nothing moves.

clue.text: Associate with retainers thrown out by force

parts.note: F is the symbol for force in physics

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Household servants are forcibly ejected by their employer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fraternise is to mix socially or be friendly with others, especially those one should keep apart from.

clue.text: Write about damming Scotland's principal river

indicators.note: a dam sits across a flow, so the about letter is set within the other letters
principal means first, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the Ribble is a river in Lancashire, north-west England
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: An essay on blocking Scotland's main river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ribble is in England, so 'Scotland's principal river' is a false trail: only S comes from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To scribble is to write hastily or carelessly.

clue.text: Cavorting nude outside, Frank gets barred

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go outside the frank word
cavorting means leaping about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: open means frank, candid

explanation.surface: A streaker frolicking in the open is kept out by the frank authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of NUDE gives UNED, which goes 'outside' OPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A barred door is closed and fastened, so it stays unopened.

clue.text: Hold up small seed container from species of Primula

parts.note: to bear a weight is to hold it up, support it
an ear is the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant

explanation.surface: Someone holds up a tiny seed pod taken from a primrose plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bear's ear is the auricula, an alpine primrose whose leaves are said to resemble a bear's ear.

clue.text: About to make trouble in government

parts.note: to concern someone is to trouble or worry them

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to stir up trouble within the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerning is a preposition meaning regarding or on the subject of, just as about is.

clue.text: Start to rubbish efforts right away

indicators.note: to rubbish is to trash, so the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
away means the right letter is removed from the word efforts

explanation.surface: Someone begins dismissing others' work out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from EFFORTS leaves EFFOTS, which 'to rubbish' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off is a phrasal verb meaning begin a journey, start out.

clue.text: End of deplorable spectacle

definitions.meaning: an end or aim, the goal of an action
Chambers gives a pitiable or ridiculous sight as one sense

explanation.surface: The finish of a dreadful show.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a purpose aimed at and, in dated use, a sorry-looking sight.

clue.text: Thought of something done to frame Peto

indicators.note: to frame is to surround, so the deed word encloses the setter

parts.note: a deed is something done, an act
the setter of the puzzle refers to himself, so Peto is me

explanation.surface: The setter believes something was done to frame him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peto' is this puzzle's setter, so the name means ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Deemed means considered or judged, the past tense of a verb of thinking.

clue.text: Corrupt umpire is troubled

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so the letters of the official are disordered

explanation.surface: A match official on the take is uneasy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Impure means morally tainted or debased, an adjectival synonym of corrupt.

clue.text: Me and Abel jogging around ship getting fit together

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters go round the ship letters
jogging means jolting or shaking, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Two friends go for a run round a ship to get into shape together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogging' and 'getting fit' paint an exercise picture; the shuffled pair of names gives AEMBLE, which goes 'around' the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble a kit is to fit its parts together into a whole.

clue.text: Military standard of old queen displayed in Britain

indicators.note: the queen is shown inside the Britain abbreviation

parts.note: BR is an abbreviation for Britain or British
Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: A regimental flag of a former monarch is put on show in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a flag or standard, such as one carried by an army in battle.

clue.text: Seconds away from emulsion spilling on length of floor covering

indicators.note: spilling paint scatters it, so the remaining letters are jumbled
the seconds letter goes away from the paint word, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: Paint spills briefly across the length of a floor covering.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S from EMULSION leaves EMULION, which 'spilling' rearranges; it sits 'on' (after) L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lino, short for this word, is a hard-wearing sheet flooring made from linseed oil and cork.

clue.text: Last to finish and certain to lose a bit of self-confidence

parts.note: an end is a finish, the close of something

indicators.note: to lose means the word for certain drops a letter

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A competitor coming last loses a little of his assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective (final) but is the verb: survive, hold out.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or survive over time, the same as enduring.

clue.text: Unlucky to be badly entertained in recital

parts.note: ill means badly, as in 'ill-treated'

indicators.note: in recital means as spoken, so the word is given by its pronunciation

parts.note: feted means lavishly entertained or celebrated

explanation.surface: A performer has bad luck at a concert where they are poorly hosted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-fated means doomed to misfortune, destined for bad luck.
